definitions.explanation: An imaginary line running from the North Pole to the South Pole on a globe or map, used to measure longitude. The prime meridian (0 degrees) passes through Greenwich, England.

examples.japanese: {経線|けいせん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{南北|なんぼく}→南北：04287_nanboku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧。
examples.english: Meridians run from north to south.

examples.japanese: ⟦{地図|ちず}→地図：02914_chizu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{経線|けいせん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{緯線|いせん}→緯線：26195_isen⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{描|えが}かれている→描く：02013_egaku⟧。
examples.english: Meridians and parallels are drawn on the map.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{標準時|ひょうじゅんじ}→標準時：18871_hyoujunji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{東経|とうけい}→東経：10004_toukei⟧135⟦{度|ど}→〜度：09845_do⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{経線|けいせん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{基準|きじゅん}→基準：00228_kijun⟧にして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Japan Standard Time is based on the meridian at 135 degrees east longitude.

notes:
Composed of {経|けい} (longitude; passing through) and ⟦{線|せん}→線：09901_sen⟧ (line). A fundamental geography term taught in schools. Always used in contrast with ⟦{緯線|いせん}→緯線：26195_isen⟧ (parallel, line of latitude), and the pair is essential for understanding maps and global coordinates.

Note the homophone ⟦{罫線|けいせん}→罫線：13865_keisen⟧ (ruled line), which has the same reading but a completely different meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経線|けいせん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{緯線|いせん}→緯線：26195_isen⟧: meridians and parallels
- {本初|ほんしょ}⟦{子午線|しごせん}→子午線：26054_shigosen⟧: prime meridian (0 degrees)
- ⟦{東経|とうけい}→東経：10004_toukei⟧…⟦{度|ど}→〜度：09845_do⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{経線|けいせん}: the meridian at … degrees east longitude
- {日付変更線|ひづけへんこうせん}: International Date Line

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{緯線|いせん}→緯線：26195_isen⟧: parallel, line of latitude — runs east-west; the counterpart to {経線|けいせん}
- ⟦{子午線|しごせん}→子午線：26054_shigosen⟧: meridian — a more formal or literary synonym
- ⟦{経度|けいど}→経度：00209_keido⟧: longitude — the numerical measurement, not the line itself
